title: Press Release: Democratic Backsliding Reaches Western Democracies, with U.S. Decline "Unprecedented" (Democracy Report 2026)
key_claim: Six of the ten new autocratizing countries in the 2026 Democracy Report are in Europe and North America; the liberal aspects of democracy - rule of law, checks and balances - are the second most common target, deteriorating in 22 countries, via politicising oversight bodies and the civil service and intimidating the judiciary.
notes: Primary democracy-monitoring research. Tier 1 anchor for the institutional-target framing of the signal.

title: Freedom in the World 2026: The Growing Shadow of Autocracy
key_claim: Global freedom declined for the 20th consecutive year in 2025, with 54 countries deteriorating and 35 improving; media freedom, freedom of personal expression and due process have suffered the heaviest impacts over two decades.
notes: Primary democracy-monitoring research; corroborates the institutional-erosion pattern.

publisher: German Marshall Fund of the United States
title: Poland's Rule-of-Law Repair: Trapped in Institutional Paralysis?
key_claim: Two years after a change of government, Poland's rule-of-law repair remains at an early stage and is 'effectively paralyzed' on judicial-independence institutions, constrained by the depth of institutional damage, presidential cohabitation and a Constitutional Tribunal that remains an illiberal veto player.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6m band): canonical evidence that institutional capture does not reverse cleanly with a change of government.

title: Europe's Democratic Backsliding Is Spreading Like Malware
key_claim: Slovakia's Fico government dismantled the Whistleblower Protection Office, restructured public broadcasting and pushed constitutional changes challenging EU legal primacy; Poland 'ran the program for eight years' and its institutional repair is 'a project measured in decades, not election cycles'; EU rule-of-law mechanisms 'can only punish after capture has already happened'.
notes: Articulates the consensus-vs-signal pivot: the problem is the technique and the institutional residue, not only who wins elections.

title: What Orban's departure means for Hungary and for Europe
key_claim: Even with a two-thirds supermajority, Hungary's new government inherits a state in which the president, prosecutor general, central bank head, State Audit Office, Media Authority, the Curia and the full Constitutional Court are stacked with the outgoing party's appointees; the Commission 'should learn from its experience with Poland', whose repair difficulties show the danger of rewarding reform before results.
notes: Live post-election case: institutional residue persists across a decisive electoral turnover.

publisher: Carnegie Europe (Carnegie Endowment for International Peace)
title: Is the Radical-Right Threat to Europe Existential or Overstated?
key_claim: The mainstream debate frames the radical-right question as a binary - 'existential or overstated' - centred on electoral momentum across forthcoming national elections from Hungary to France.
notes: Establishes the consensus framing the signal sits beneath - the electoral horse-race lens.

title: Peter Magyar wins Hungary election, unseating Viktor Orban after 16 years
key_claim: Tisza won 138 of 199 parliamentary seats on 53.6% of the vote, a two-thirds majority; the extent of reform 'will depend on whether Tisza secures the two-thirds constitutional majority it would need to reverse much of Orban's legacy'.
notes: Primary reporting of the April 2026 Hungarian election result - the headline event the signal reframes.
